snippet.title: "Every Call Ends the Same Way..."
snippet.description:
Download your free scaling roadmap here: https://www.acquisition.com/roadmap-yt-d

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com, which is a platform for people to build communities online, making a living doing what they love, with people like them.
36 yrs old: I did a $106M book launch selling 3.6M copies of my $100M Money Models book, in 72 hours, breaking the Guinness world record for the fastest selling non-fiction book of all time.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex

snippet.title: AI agent that creates Twitter threads in minutes
snippet.description:
Just built an AI agent that creates Twitter threads in minutes. No more staring at blank screens.

Here's what I learned: Context beats complexity every time.

I used Claude with a Twitter MCP server and one simple prompt template. The magic wasn't in fancy code - it was in teaching the AI the thread structure: hook, main points, recap, CTA.

Setup took 10 minutes:
• Added Twitter API keys
• Created a markdown template 
• Connected the MCP server

Result? My AI now writes 6-tweet threads about complex topics while I grab coffee.

The real insight: Your AI is only as good as the context you give it. Feed it clear structure and examples, and it'll deliver consistent results.

What repetitive content tasks are eating your time? Sometimes the simplest automation wins.

Tax firms are under pressure from more than deadlines. They are also dealing with the hidden cost of manual tax payment workflows: cash, time, and stress.

In this Miles Masterclass course, AI-Powered Transformation in Tax Firms, Solon Angel explores how AI can modernize tax payment workflows, reduce administrative burden, and help firms deliver a more secure and scalable client experience.

The course begins by examining the problems with traditional tax payment processes, including paper checks, clunky portals, late fees, fraud exposure, fragmented systems, and burnout for both accounting teams and clients.

snippet.description:

You run your profit and loss report and it shows everything your business did last month. Revenue, expenses, profit. Great. But here's the problem: it's all mixed together in one giant blob. You can't tell which location made the most money. You can't see which project went over budget. You can't figure out which business line is actually profitable and which one is dragging you down. Your chart of accounts only shows WHAT happened. It doesn't show WHERE it happened. That's the entire point of classes in QuickBooks. Classes let you tag every single transaction so you can slice your financials any way you want: by department, by location, by project, by product line, whatever matters to YOUR business. In this video, I'm walking you through 8 different Excel dashboards that show you how to analyze your business by class.

What you'll learn in this video:
- Setting up QuickBooks class tracking so every transaction gets tagged
- Building a profit and loss dashboard organized by class instead of just accounts
- Creating Excel formulas that automatically filter your data by class
- Making reports that compare performance across different classes and time periods
- Using pivot tables to click and expand from high level summaries down to individual transactions
- Adding checkboxes so you can instantly show or hide specific classes
- Building a budget vs actual dashboard broken out by class
- Creating a KPI dashboard where you pick which classes to analyze

snippet.title: Advanced Excel Masterclass by Cristiano Galvao | Miles Masterclass Trailer
snippet.description:
Excel remains one of the most powerful tools in finance, but modern finance teams need more than spreadsheets. They need scalable systems for analysis, reporting, and decision-making.

In this Miles Masterclass course, Advanced Excel Masterclass, Cristiano Galvao demonstrates how finance professionals can transform Excel into a high-performance platform for managing large datasets, automating workflows, and delivering better business insights.

The course begins by addressing one of the biggest challenges in finance: handling massive volumes of data. Learners will see how tools such as Power Query and the Excel Data Model can help manage millions of records efficiently while maintaining speed, accuracy, and performance.

Cristiano then focuses on building structured and repeatable workflows. Participants learn how to automate data preparation, standardize inconsistent inputs, create reusable financial summaries, and establish reporting processes that maintain consistency across multiple reports and reporting periods.

The course also explores interactive dashboards using PivotTables, Pivot Charts, slicers, and timelines, helping finance teams move beyond static reports and create dynamic reporting environments that support real-time decision-making.

In the final modules, learners strengthen their analytical capabilities with advanced Excel functions including SUMIFS, XLOOKUP, LET, and LAMBDA. The course also demonstrates how AI-powered Excel features can help identify patterns, surface insights, and accelerate financial analysis.

Watch the full course here to learn how to automate reporting, improve financial analysis, and build scalable Excel workflows that support modern finance operations.

snippet.title: 8 Entrepreneurs Compete For $100,000 - Episode 1
snippet.description:
Download your free scaling roadmap here: https://www.acquisition.com/roadmap-yta509

If you’re new to my channel, my name is Alex Hormozi. I’m the founder and managing partner of Acquisition.com. It’s a family office, which is just a formal way of saying we invest our own money into companies. Our 10 portfolio companies bring in over $250,000,000+ per year. Our ownership stake varies between 20% and 100% of them. Given this is a YT channel, and anyone can claim anything, I’ll give you some stuff you can google to verify below.

How I got here…

21: Graduated Vanderbilt in 3 years Magna Cum Laude, and took a fancy consulting job.
23 yrs old: Left my fancy consulting job to start a business (a gym).
24 yrs old: Opened 5 gym locations.
26 yrs old: Closed down 6th gym. Lost everything. 
26 yrs old: Got back to launching gyms (launched 33). Then, lost everything for a 2nd time. 
26 yrs old: In desperation, started licensing model as a hail mary. It worked. 
27 yrs old: "Gym Launch" does $3M profit the next 6 months. Then $17M profit next 12 months.
28 yrs old: Started Prestige Labs. $20M the first year.  
29 yrs old: Launched ALAN, a software company for agencies to work leads for customers. Scaled to $1.7mmo within 6 months. 
31 yrs old: Sold 75% of UseAlan to a strategic buyer in an all stock deal. 
31 yrs old: Sold 66% of Gym Launch & Prestige Labs at $46.2M valuation in all-cash deal to American Pacific Group. (you can google it)
31 yrs old: Started our family office Acquisition.com. We invest and scale companies using the $42M in distributions we had taken + the cash from the $46.2M exit.
32 yrs old: Started making free content showing how we grow companies to make real business education accessible to everyone (and) to attract business owners to invest or scale their businesses. 
34 yrs old: I became co-owner of https://Skool.com, which is a platform for people to build communities online, making a living doing what they love, with people like them.
36 yrs old: I did a $106M book launch selling 3.6M copies of my $100M Money Models book, in 72 hours, breaking the Guinness world record for the fastest selling non-fiction book of all time.

Today: Our portfolio now does $200M/yr between 10 companies. The largest doing $100M/yr the smallest doing $5M per year. Our ownership varies between 20% and 100% ownership of the companies. Many of them we invested in early and helped grow (which is how we make our money - not youtube videos).

To all the gladiators in the arena, we’re all in the middle of writing our own stories. The worse the monsters, the more epic the story.

You either get an epic outcome or an epic story. Both mean you win. 

Keep crushing. May your desires be greater than your obstacles. 

Never quit,

Alex
